title: Find missing values with IS NULL
description: The `employees` table has a `manager_id` column that is NULL for anyone with no manager. Write a query that returns the `first_name` and `last_name` of every employee with no manager.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: IS NULL
NULL means 'no value', and it can't be compared with = the way normal values can (manager_id = NULL never matches anything) - IS NULL is the dedicated check for it.
Select first_name and last_name from employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL.
expected_behavior: Returns the employees whose manager_id is NULL.
solution: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL;
explanation: NULL represents the absence of a value, so ordinary equality doesn't apply to it - SQL has IS NULL and IS NOT NULL specifically because `= NULL` would silently match nothing at all, a common early mistake.
